name: Tomasz Wierzbicki
equipment: Leather jacket, cracked, with a Solidarnosc pin inside the lapel
Hunting/sniper rifle (Steyr SSG 69) with Kahles scope, 5 rounds loaded, broken down in a cello case
Zeiss 10x50 binoculars, East German, bought in a Warsaw flea market
Hand-drawn street maps of three cities in a school exercise book
A pouch of rolling tobacco and a Zippo
A rosary that belonged to his grandmother, which he does not use and does not take off
Cover passport: Tomas Wirth, Austrian, piano tuner and cello repairer (weak legend: real trade, forged papers, he cannot tune a piano)
features: Versatility (Human origin: +1 to all ability scores)
Overwatch (reaction: when an enemy he can see moves within his weapon's normal range, make one ranged attack against it; 1 per short rest)
Trailwise (advantage on Survival checks to track and navigate, city or country; the party cannot be surprised while he is on watch and conscious)
Steady Aim (bonus action, if he has not moved this turn: advantage on his next ranged attack, speed 0 until end of turn)
Nobody's Man (Drifter background: he can find a bed, a meal and a back door in any working-class district in Central Europe, and people there forget his face on request)

personality.traits: I am quiet, watchful and badly fed, and I make jokes so dark the others are never sure they were jokes. I sleep anywhere and wake instantly. I hate being indoors for more than a day.
personality.ideals: The Russians stole my country twice in one century. I do not need a better reason, and I do not need anyone's flag but ours.
personality.bonds: My sister Agnieszka is in Gdansk, interned in 1982 and released, and still printing leaflets in a basement. Every dollar I earn that I do not eat goes to her press.
personality.flaws: I hate them, not just the system but the men, and one day I will have a Russian in my scope who could be allowed to live, and I am not sure what I will do.

appearance: A lean, hollow-cheeked Pole of twenty-nine with cropped fair hair, pale eyes, a three-day beard that is always three days, and a cello case he carries like it weighs nothing. He looks hungry because he usually is. He has a paratrooper's way of landing on the balls of his feet when he steps off a tram.
backstory: Tomasz Wierzbicki was a sergeant in the 6th Airborne Brigade, a sniper and a cross-country runner, until 13 December 1981, when martial law came and his unit was put on the streets of Krakow against people his own age. He deserted that night, walked south through the Tatras in the snow with a rifle he later threw in a river, and crossed into Czechoslovakia and then Austria over nine days he describes as 'a holiday'. The Austrians interned him; the Annex got him out of a refugee camp at Traiskirchen because he could recognise every unit insignia in the Warsaw Pact at four hundred metres. He is the team's long eye: overwatch on meets, counter-surveillance, the man on the roof. He would follow Sofia anywhere. He thinks Julian is ridiculous and would die for him, and he has not decided yet how he feels about helping a KGB colonel to a comfortable life in the West.
